title: Solarpunk community center
lede: A miners’ memorial statue holds a wind turbine in front of a community centre that retrains miners as turbine technicians.
summary: Bronze miners with a wind turbine before a solar-fitted community centre, in clear daylight. The.lemonaut.ukr, 2024.

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the Commons file (original 2284 × 2823 px PNG, viewed at 1295 × 1600 px).

styles.note: A solarpunk scene about a just transition: a turbine, solar panels, a public building, and a blue sky. Partial fit: the palette is warm orange and bronze more than leaf green.

context: The uploader describes it as a digital illustration of a solarpunk community centre that provides re-specialization for miners so that they can become wind turbine technicians. It is dated 5 July 2024. [Commons file page](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Solarpunk_community_center.png).
observed: In the foreground, a bronze statue of a miner in a helmet and harness pulls a second miner out of a manhole. The standing figure holds a small three-bladed wind turbine like a staff, and a pickaxe lies on the ground.
A girl in an orange coat with a yellow helmet and a paper in her hand looks at the statue.
Behind, a building with orange, cream, and glass blocks carries the sign “COMMUNITY CE…”, small solar panels on brackets, and a hedge of flowering shrubs.
At left, an older brick hall has round-arched windows, and a tree has pale violet blossom.
The sky is light blue with soft white clouds. Thin dark outlines, flat colour, and a visible grain texture.
interpretation: The scene puts the politics of solarpunk (a fair transition for workers) into a civic square. Old labour and new energy share one monument.
The palette leans orange and bronze, so the image is a partial fit to the green, blue, and gold grammar. The blue sky and the visible renewables keep it in the style.
borrow: Combine a familiar civic form (a monument, a town square) with renewable technology, so the change reads as continuity.

images.alt: Illustration of a town square: a bronze statue of one miner pulling another from a manhole while holding a wind turbine, a girl in an orange coat looking up at it, and a colourful community centre with solar panels behind.
